issues.legal_issue: A civil court must refer a contested issue assigned exclusively to a tenancy authority even when that issue arises in a properly constituted suit for specific performance.
material_facts: The suit sought specific performance of agreements to sell agricultural land governed by the tenancy legislation.
The defendant contested the suit on the ground that the plaintiff was not an agriculturist and was therefore barred from purchasing the land.
The trial court and the High Court decided the plaintiff’s agriculturist status themselves, treating it as an incidental issue in the civil suit.
The legislation assigned the determination of whether a person was an agriculturist to the Mamlatdar and barred civil courts from deciding matters assigned to the statutory authorities.
issues.conclusion: The civil court lacked jurisdiction to decide the contested issue of agriculturist status and was required to stay the suit and refer that issue to the competent authority. The appeal was allowed, the decrees dismissing the suit were set aside, and the suit was remanded for further proceedings in accordance with the authority’s decision.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 70(a), 85 and 85A of the Bombay Tenancy and Agricultural Lands Act, 1948, the Mamlatdar has exclusive jurisdiction to decide whether a person is an agriculturist; when that issue arises upon contest in a civil suit, the civil court must stay the suit, refer the issue to the competent authority, and thereafter dispose of the suit consistently with its decision. Although exclusion of civil jurisdiction is not readily inferred (Secretary of State v. Mask), the express statutory bar and referral scheme require it even when the issue is incidental to a suit otherwise cognizable by a civil court. The court approved Dhondi Tukaram Mali v. Dadoo Piraji Adgale and Trimbak Sopana Girme v. Gangaram Mhataraba Yadav, and relied on Bhimaji Shanker Kulkarni v. Dundappa Vithappa Udapudi, Ishverlal Thakorelal Almaula v. Motibhai Nagjibhai, and Noor Mohd. Khan Ghouse Khan Soudagar v. Fakirappa Bharmappa Machenahalli. It explained that Jambu Rao Satappa Kocheri v. Neminath Appayya Hanammannaver concerned a different issue arising after acquisition and did not displace the rule; it also distinguished Mussamiya Imam Haider Bax Razvi v. Rabari Govindbhai Ratnabhai in light of the statutory provisions and issue there considered.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and agricultural_land_sale and contested_agriculturist_status_issue and status_question_assigned_to_exclusive_authority

predicates.specific_performance_suit: A party brought a civil suit seeking specific performance of an agreement to transfer property.
predicates.agricultural_land_sale: The agreement concerned the transfer of land used for agricultural purposes.
predicates.contested_agriculturist_status_issue: A party disputed whether the person seeking the transfer qualified as an agriculturist, and that status had to be determined to resolve the dispute.
predicates.status_question_assigned_to_exclusive_au: The governing law assigned determination of the disputed status to a designated authority rather than the civil court.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance suit concerns agricultural land and a contested eligibility issue is assigned to an exclusive authority, the civil court must stay the suit and refer that issue to the authority.
